prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: low-speed head-on collision in League City, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported neck strain. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1245; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Driver 1 was traveling westbound in the left lane on a League City roadway when the vehicle crossed the center line and struck the eastbound vehicle operated by Driver 2 nearly head-on. Both vehicles sustained front-end damage consistent with the impact described by the parties, and the crumpling of the front bumpers, hood and airbag deployment in the Driver 1 vehicle matched the force reported at the scene. Driver 1 was the policyholder of record, and Passenger was seated in the front right seat. Driver 1 stated that his head snapped forward and back during the collision and that he felt neck pain shortly afterward. Driver 2 and two independent witnesses gave consistent accounts of how the collision occurred, and their statements were supported by photographs taken at the scene. Both drivers and Passenger were identified and confirmed present in their vehicles. No prior damage to either vehicle was observed or reported by any party. Driver 1 was transported by EMS for evaluation of neck strain and released to a family member at the hospital.
